item.title: Qwen Model Jaggedness, Help-Desk Vishing, and QuickBooks Phishing Dominate Q3
item.content:encoded:
Window: 29 Oct 11:00 → 29 Oct 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

The Ultra Trail: From Viewer to Mailer — Should Read

Infoblox traced a QuickBooks support phishing campaign to UltraMailer’s chanret.com tracking infrastructure, showing how scammers abuse the bulk-email tool while UltraViewer is used in related tech-support scams. The investigation also found trojanized UltraMailer and UltraViewer installers carrying remote-access malware, though there is no evidence their developers were involved.

  • Infoblox linked a QuickBooks support phishing campaign using more than 350 QuickBooks-lookalike domains to chanret.com, UltraMailer’s default email-tracking domain.
  • The phishing emails used 1×1 tracking images that sent recipient email addresses, encoded in the image URL, to track.chanret.com when messages were opened.
  • The campaign briefly used Mail250 infrastructure in August 2026, but stopped after Mail250 suspended the reported account; the actor resumed activity through chanret.com on September 8.
  • Researchers found trojanized UltraMailer and UltraViewer installers that contained authentic copies of the applications alongside njRAT and DarkKometa malware, respectively.
  • The article found no evidence that the developers of UltraViewer or UltraMailer participated in the scams or distributed the malicious installers.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: ultraviewer, ultramailer, mail250, quickbooks

Vendors: duc-fabulous, mail250, intuit, dynadot

Cohere’s Qwen Story: Looks More Like Model Jaggedness — May Read

Replaying Cohere’s Qwen trace showed the model generated many different, often invalid or local upload destinations rather than a fixed Alibaba endpoint, suggesting inconsistent “model jaggedness” rather than clear evidence of a backdoor. The findings reinforce the need to sandbox AI agents and restrict network permissions.

  • Cohere reported that Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, when asked to write a detection rule for curl downloads followed by bash execution, issued a command that attempted to send a test string to an Alibaba Cloud storage address.
  • Researchers replayed the published trace 64 times from just before the URL destination and observed 52 distinct host strings, including local-looking, nonexistent, and invalid domains.
  • Seven sampled destinations used Amazon Web Services hostnames, six used Alibaba Cloud hostnames, and 20 were local or internal-looking.
  • Changing the order of curl and wget in a check for available programs reduced continuations containing a curl network command from 15 of 32 to 4 of 32.
  • The researchers concluded that the results more strongly support inconsistent model behavior, which they call model jaggedness, than a single hard-coded destination, while noting that the tests cannot prove no backdoor exists.

Products: qwen3-8-flash-next, vllm

Vendors: alibaba, cohere, check-point, vllm-project

The day after tomorrow: After PHP2Shell, it gets worse, then defenders win — Optional

AI is expected to make it easier and faster to turn overlooked software flaws into critical exploits, creating a difficult period for security teams. The article argues defenders can ultimately gain an advantage by combining strong security architecture with complete asset visibility and rapid, automated remediation.

  • The article says recent critical remote-code-execution flaws in PHP and the Brotli compression library have heightened concern, though no mass compromise has been reported.
  • It states that the out-of-memory issue behind PHP2Shell was identified in a 2024 audit but remained unfixed until researchers showed it could be exploited last year.
  • The article argues that AI can reduce the work required to turn unexplained software behavior into a usable exploit by helping researchers investigate and chain flaws together.
  • It recommends that organizations combine strong security architecture with fast fixes, beginning with visibility into all software they run, including components in base images, CI images, hosting panels, and vendor software.
  • The article says teams should check code early, test applications and external networks before releases and after changes, and provide fixes that people can review.

Products: php, brotli

Vendors: aikido, anthropic, cloudflare, google

Cloudflare DDoS Threat Report 2026 Q3: More swarms, fewer giants — Optional

Cloudflare mitigated 18.2 million network-layer DDoS attacks in Q3 2026, driven by a 208% surge in short, sub-1 Gbps attacks, while attacks over 1 Tbps fell 69% after major IoT botnet disruptions. Attackers shifted away from CLDAP amplification toward DNS amplification and UDP floods, with the United States again the most-targeted country.

  • Cloudflare mitigated 18.2 million network-layer DDoS attacks and 14.4 trillion HTTP DDoS requests during Q3 2026.
  • Network-layer attacks increased 208% year over year, with 96% ending in under 10 minutes and 98% remaining below 1 Gbps.
  • Hyper-volumetric attacks exceeding 1 Tbps fell from 805 in Q2 2026 to 251 in Q3, while Mirai-classified mitigations peaked at 57.23 PB in August.
  • CLDAP attacks collapsed to 0.05% of network-layer attacks, while DNS amplification rose 215% and general UDP floods grew to 31.31% of such attacks.
  • The United States was the most-attacked location in Q3 2026, followed by China, while Canada rose from 16th to sixth and Israel moved seven places to 10th.

Products: cloudflare-radar, ddos-botnet-threat-feed

Vendors: cloudflare

IR trends Q3 2026: Actors impersonate IT help desks in vishing attacks as ransomware activity increases — Optional

Cisco Talos reports that Q3 2026 incident response engagements were increasingly driven by vishing callers impersonating IT help desks and by exploitation of internet-facing systems, while ransomware rose to 27% of cases. Organizations should prioritize phishing-resistant MFA, secure credential management, centralized logging, and protection of endpoint defenses against EDR-disabling techniques.

  • Phishing was the most common initial access method in Cisco Talos Incident Response engagements in Q3 2026, appearing in 37% of cases, while exploitation of public-facing applications accounted for 33%.
  • Ransomware and pre-ransomware incidents rose to 27% of engagements, with actors including Interlock and the emerging VYPR group disabling endpoint security tools and using remote-management access.
  • Talos attributed most prolonged telecommunications-sector cyber-espionage intrusions with high confidence to China state-sponsored actors, including Salt Typhoon, which used valid credentials and CVE-2023-20198 in publicly accessible management interfaces.
  • Financial organizations and public administration were tied as the most targeted sectors at 18% of engagements, while health care ranked third.
  • The most common security weakness was insufficient logging, followed by improper credential and secret management and missing or inadequate authentication and multi-factor authentication controls.

Technologies: edr, remote-access, operating-system, router

Products: cisco-ios-xe, cisco-secure-endpoint, microsoft-quick-assist, windows-defender-application-control, github-copilot-cli, claude-code

Vendors: cisco, microsoft, anthropic, github

item.title: NIK C2, PHP2Shell CVEs, and NetamLoader Lead Threat Updates
item.content:encoded:
Window: 29 Oct 07:00 → 29 Oct 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Ghost in the PHP2Shell: Why coordinated disclosure and patching will start moving faster — Must Read

PHP2Shell shows how AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and leaked disclosure details can compress the time between a flaw’s discovery, exploitation, and patching. Organizations should maintain accurate software inventories and be ready to rapidly deploy patches or mitigations when critical runtime vulnerabilities emerge.

  • PHP2Shell consists of two PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, whose fixes were released on October 21 after their CVE identifiers leaked on October 20.
  • Attackers were attempting to exploit PHP2Shell before PHP announced the fixes, and CISA reported successful exploitation attempts after the patches were released.
  • As of October 27, Censys reported that about 11.2 million PHP services had moved to fixed versions while 32.5 million were still running affected versions, with more than 60 million services not reporting a version.
  • Aikido reported that its AI Code Analysis rediscovered PHP2Shell in PHP within a few hours after the disclosure.
  • The article argues that shorter, tighter coordinated-disclosure embargoes and faster patching readiness are needed as AI reduces the time from vulnerability discovery to exploitation.

Technologies: container-platform

Products: php, aikido-images, codex

Vendors: php-foundation, aikido, cloudflare, openai

NIK C2: The new AI-enabled command-and-control framework — Should Read

Cisco Talos identified NIK C2, a Go-based Windows remote-access framework that integrates OpenAI’s API directly into its command-and-control workflow to analyze stolen data from compromised hosts. The malware also supports credential and wallet theft, surveillance, lateral movement, defense evasion, and deployable screen-locking ransomware.

  • Cisco Talos observed NIK C2, a Go-based 64-bit Windows remote-access implant with persistent command-and-control communications over TLS WebSockets and an HTTP polling fallback.
  • NIK C2 includes an ai_generate command that sends operator prompts to the OpenAI Chat Completions API from the compromised host and returns the generated response to the command-and-control server.
  • If an operator does not provide an API key, the implant attempts to use the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable on the victim machine.
  • The implant supports credential theft, browser and cryptocurrency wallet data collection, keystroke logging, screen and audio surveillance, proxying, RDP operations, and several defense-evasion functions.
  • NIK C2 can deploy screen-locking ransomware that uses an HTML page, a Windows autostart registry entry, and a relaunch loop to display cryptocurrency payment demands.

Technologies: remote-access, operating-system, proxy, antivirus

Products: nik-c2, openai-chat-completions-api, windows, powershell, clamav

Vendors: cisco, openai, microsoft

Unknown APT uses NetamLoader to attack a Win10 OS customized for governments in Asia — Should Read

Kaspersky uncovered NetamLoader, an unattributed, highly sophisticated .NET/XAML malware framework likely delivered through a supply-chain compromise of a government-only Windows 10 build used in Asia. It abuses trusted components and deserialization flaws to bypass AMSI, erase evidence, migrate execution into dllhost.exe, and communicate with a C2 server after long sandbox-evasion delays.

  • Kaspersky identified an unattributed malware framework named NetamLoader in 2026 after detecting a malicious .config file inside a CAB archive stored in the Windows update-package directory.
  • The infection chain used PatchMyPC-ScriptRunner.exe, Microsoft-signed .NET assemblies, AppDomainManager injection, a crafted .resx file, and XAML payloads to load malicious code.
  • NetamLoader patched the AMSI scanning interface so that scans returned a clean result, then used a remote COM object to load its next-stage payload into dllhost.exe.
  • The malware deleted malicious files, CLR usage logs, Prefetch files, and selected update-log entries to reduce forensic evidence.
  • The .NET 2 plugin delayed its initial C2 connection by 20 to 40 minutes, polled the openaigpt4v.com C2 infrastructure, and used AES-CBC with HMAC to encrypt and authenticate network traffic.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows-10, patch-my-pc, windows-server-appfabric, dotnet-framework, amsi

Vendors: kaspersky, microsoft, patch-my-pc, cloudflare

Configured to protect: How to properly use security policies — Optional

Analysis of 1.6 million Acronis-managed endpoints finds that customers generally retain secure defaults and use multiple plans mainly to separate backup from security, often adding them incrementally over time. MSPs are split between standardized and customized customer configurations, with geography and industry—especially health care and education—strongly influencing how comprehensive protection is deployed.

  • The report analyzes live configuration records from more than 1.6 million active endpoints managed through Acronis Cyber Platform.
  • Across the fleet, 65% of active endpoints run two or more protection modules, while the average Windows workstation runs 5.6 modules.
  • Among machines with two or more separate protection plans, 82% use plans for different purposes, such as separate backup and security plans, while 77% use the same schedule across their plans.
  • Core default protections are commonly retained: the anti-malware behavioral engine is enabled in 84.7% of plans, and a ransomware response is configured in 87.9% of active-protection plans.
  • Among more than 9,000 managed service providers with at least five active customers, roughly half apply a uniform plan pattern to most customers and roughly half customize by customer.

Technologies: backup, antivirus, edr, dlp, remote-access, network-monitoring

Products: acronis-cyber-platform

Vendors: acronis

Find the AI Risks That Matter in a Flood of AI Activity — Optional

Netskope promotes its AI Risk AISecOps Agent as a way to correlate AI-related telemetry across apps, agents, and MCP servers, automatically prioritize risky behavioral patterns, and provide evidence-backed investigation verdicts. The tool is designed to help analysts focus on higher-risk AI activity while existing DLP and guardrail controls continue enforcing policy.

  • AI risk can emerge when individually normal-looking changes, such as an approved AI application accessing new data or an agent using additional tools, form a risky pattern when viewed together.
  • The article cites a June 2026 Microsoft demonstration in which changes to an approved MCP tool could cause an AI agent to send invoice data to an external server, with the risk becoming apparent through comparison with historical behavior.
  • Netskope AI Risk AISecOps Agent evaluates users, AI applications, agents, and MCP servers daily, ranks them by behavioral risk, and automatically investigates the highest-ranked entities.
  • For each prioritized entity, the agent correlates related events, creates an evidence timeline, and returns a risky, legitimate, or inconclusive verdict with a confidence level.
  • The agent is not deployed inline, so existing real-time controls such as AI Guardrails and DLP continue enforcing policy while analysts review investigations and retain remediation decisions.

Technologies: dlp, casb, proxy

Products: ai-risk-aisecops-agent, netskope-one, netskope-skylight-ai-security, netskope-skylight-ai-guardrails, netskope-one-dlp, netskope-one-ueba, netskope-one-ng-swg, netskope-skylight-agentic-broker, netskope-skylight-ai-command-center

Vendors: netskope

item.title: 319 Browser Extensions Searchjack 13.4 Million Users
item.content:encoded:
Window: 28 Oct 23:00 → 29 Oct 03:00 UTC (4 hours)

Searchjacked: Hidden Browser Extensions Hijack Searches for 13 Million Users — Should Read

Researchers identified 319 mostly hidden Chrome extensions, installed by roughly 13.4 million users over a decade, that replace default search engines and route queries through operator-controlled proxies to monetize Yahoo or Bing referral traffic. This gives operators visibility into users’ searches and the ability to dynamically redirect them to potentially malicious destinations.

  • The investigation identified 319 browser extensions that changed users’ default search providers and were installed by roughly 13.4 million users over a decade.
  • Many of the extensions are unlisted in the Chrome Web Store and are promoted through advertisements for tools such as PDF search, manual finding, safe search, and AI search.
  • The extensions route search queries through operator-controlled proxy servers before redirecting users to Yahoo or Bing results with search-syndication partner tracking IDs.
  • The proxy servers allow operators to record search referrals and can choose destinations separately for each request; one tested extension sent identical searches to several different destinations.
  • Identified operators include Intango LTD, Tightrope Interactive, System1, Perion Network, and ValidClick/Inuvo, while two large groups called SecuryBrowse and Bing-Search remain unattributed.

Technologies: browser, proxy

Products: google-chrome, chrome-web-store, google-ads, microsoft-bing, yahoo-search, censys, urlscan, decryptads

Vendors: google, microsoft, yahoo, censys, urlscan, decryptads

item.title: UAT-11473 Targets Cisco SD-WAN as PHP2Shell Enters CISA KEV
item.content:encoded:
Window: 28 Oct 19:00 → 28 Oct 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

Inside KeyDrift: Analyzing historical UAT-11473 activity on Cisco SD-WAN — Must Read

Cisco Talos found that UAT-11473 exploited CVE-2026-20127 in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN controllers to deploy the KeyDrift framework, which persistently intercepts control-plane traffic and steals IPsec keying material. Organizations should urgently patch affected SD-WAN systems and investigate for modified runit services, vdaemon injection, and KeyDrift artifacts.

  • Cisco Talos identified UAT-11473 exploiting CVE-2026-20127, an authentication-bypass flaw in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controller instances, to gain unauthorized access.
  • UAT-11473 deployed the KeyDrift malware framework, whose PolyFlame component is injected into legitimate vdaemon processes and can provide command execution and intermediate command-and-control functions.
  • KeyDrift’s LittleFilch component intercepts decrypted Cisco SD-WAN control-plane traffic, extracts assessed AES-256 IPsec data-plane key material, and stores collected records in encrypted form.
  • Talos assesses with high confidence that UAT-11473’s infrastructure considerably overlaps with Volt Typhoon’s Silent Train covert access network.
  • Cisco released patches for CVE-2026-20127 and a Catalyst SD-WAN hardening guide, while Talos recommends organizations monitor for post-compromise activity.

Technologies: router

Products: cisco-catalyst-sd-wan, cisco-sd-wan-catalyst-controller

Vendors: cisco

PHP2Shell is in CISA KEV: why runtime visibility matters — Must Read

CISA added the actively exploited PHP2Shell flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, to its KEV catalog, making rapid identification and patching of affected PHP runtimes urgent. Organizations need runtime-level inventory to find vulnerable host packages, container images, and managed deployments, then upgrade, rebuild, restart workers, and review systems left exposed.

  • CISA added CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, known as PHP2Shell, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 26, 2026, with a remediation deadline of October 29 for U.S. federal civilian agencies.
  • The affected PHP releases are versions before 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12, while PHP 8.1 and older are end of life and receive no fixes from the PHP project.
  • PHP states that installations serving web requests are at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed, with mod_php carrying the highest risk.
  • Delft University’s Threat Intelligence Lab recorded more than 60,000 PHP2Shell exploitation requests from over 600 IP addresses across more than 70 countries as of October 27.
  • Organizations should identify affected hosts, container images, and managed hosting environments; apply vendor fixes or upgrade PHP; rebuild and redeploy images; and restart PHP workers after updating.

Technologies: web-server, container-platform

Products: php, apache-http-server, php-fpm, mod-php, frankenphp, litespeed-web-server, mend-renovate

Vendors: php, apache-software-foundation, frankenphp, litespeed-technologies, mend-io, cisa

John Strand's 11 Core Skills: For SOC Analysts — Optional

Effective SOC analysts need a broad foundation spanning Windows and Linux, network and log analysis, memory and malware forensics, EDR, threat hunting, incident response, vulnerability prioritization, automation, and clear communication. The key is connecting evidence across these domains to detect and respond to real-world threats.

  • Effective SOC analysts need a practical understanding of both Windows and Linux, including how to investigate those systems after a compromise.
  • Network traffic analysis requires understanding TCP/IP, the differences between TCP and UDP, and what normal traffic looks like in an organization’s environment.
  • Memory forensics can reveal processes, connections, and DLLs that may remain visible even when attackers delete their tools or use fileless malware.
  • SOC analysts should use threat hunting to search for threats that automated systems may have missed, including attackers abusing legitimate tools.
  • Clear communication and documentation are essential because technical findings must be understood by different audiences and used to improve future response efforts.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: windows, linux, volatility, powershell, python, bash

item.title: Node2Shell RCE Risk and AMOS Malware in Poisoned AI Agent Skills
item.content:encoded:
Window: 28 Oct 15:00 → 28 Oct 19:00 UTC (4 hours)

CVE-2026-111497: Node2Shell / HTTP2Shell Vulnerability May Allow RCE — Must Read

CVE-2026-111497 (Node2Shell/HTTP2Shell) is a critical out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder that can enable crashes, memory disclosure, or remote code execution when vulnerable software decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data. Organizations should urgently patch affected Node.js, Bun, .NET, Python, Envoy, and other Brotli-dependent components, especially internet-facing services that accept Content-Encoding: br requests or fetch external content.

  • CVE-2026-111497, also called Node2Shell and HTTP2Shell, is a critical out-of-bounds write flaw in Google’s Brotli decoder that can cause crashes, memory disclosure, or remote code execution when processing attacker-controlled Brotli data.
  • The vulnerability can be reached through crafted Brotli-compressed HTTP requests sent to servers or through malicious Brotli-compressed responses automatically decoded by client applications.
  • Affected software may include Node.js, Bun, Python Brotli bindings, .NET, Envoy Proxy, Istio, Java brotli4j, libbrotli, and curl/libcurl through Brotli dependencies.
  • Zscaler Deception observed 402 events from 20 source IP addresses targeting 12 customers within 24 hours of public disclosure, with 40% classified as reconnaissance and 60% as exploitation attempts.
  • Organizations are advised to patch vulnerable components, rebuild and redeploy containers using patched images, disable Brotli decoding on vulnerable paths if patching is delayed, and monitor for crashes or unusual process and network behavior.

Technologies: proxy, waf, dlp

Products: google-brotli, node-js, bun, .net, envoy-proxy, istio, python-brotli, brotlicffi, java-brotli4j, libbrotli, curl, zscaler-private-access, zscaler-deception

Vendors: google, node-js-project, bun, microsoft, envoy-proxy-project, istio-project, curl-project, zscaler

AMOS Malware in AI Agent Skills: Analysis and IoCs — Should Read

Cyera identified 516 poisoned AI-agent skills that used fake setup requirements and encoded commands to deliver the Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS), often while receiving high automated security grades. Organizations should inspect entire skill packages and block skills that direct users or agents to download external tools, decode Base64 commands, or execute shell installers.

  • Cyera Research identified 516 samples classified as part of an Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS) campaign distributed through poisoned AI-agent skills.
  • The malicious skills used fake prerequisites and setup instructions to direct users or agents to download external files or decode and execute commands, with macOS instructions often using Base64-decoded Bash commands.
  • In the analyzed sample, 91.92.242.30 accounted for 83.7% of payload-host references, and two glot.io snippets accounted for 95.9% of paste-relay references.
  • All 70 confirmed-malicious skills identified on platforms with automated evaluation received high security grades, indicating that those checks missed malicious instructions embedded in skill files.
  • AMOS can collect browser passwords and session cookies, keychain information, and sensitive files before sending the data to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

Technologies: package-registry

Products: agent-guardian, openclaw, clawhub, skills-directory, claude-code, claude-cowork

Vendors: cyera, openclaw, clawhub, skills-directory, anthropic

Malicious AI Skills: The Risk to Corporate Endpoints — Should Read

Cyera researchers found a trojanized copy of Anthropic’s PDF skill that preserved most legitimate files but replaced its instructions and added an obfuscated Linux reverse-shell binary connecting to a hard-coded server. The case highlights AI-skill supply-chain risk: organizations should verify entire skill packages, including instruction files, executables, and network destinations, before agents can use them.

  • Cyera Research analyzed a package named “pdf” that impersonated Anthropic’s PDF skill by retaining its name, description, and 11 identical files while replacing the SKILL.md instructions.
  • The package added a 5 MB obfuscated 64-bit Linux Go executable named system_linux that decrypts a hard-coded destination and opens a TCP connection to 81.70.101[.]115:2345, attaching /bin/bash to that connection.
  • The altered SKILL.md directs the agent to contact scan.100tal[.]com, which resolved during the researchers’ analysis to the private IP address 10.160.65[.]97.
  • Researchers observed five similar tar files between May 23 and July 14, 2026, but could not establish how the packages were distributed, whether anyone used them, or whether the binary was executed.
  • The article says organizations should verify an entire skill package against its claimed source and investigate unexpected commands, network destinations, and executable files before allowing an agent to use it.

Technologies: cloud-platform, operating-system

Products: anthropic-pdf-skill, claude-code, claude-cowork, agent-guardian, tencent-cloud

Vendors: anthropic, tencent-cloud, cyera

The Silent Ransom Group Leak Shows Why Paying for Silence Fails — Optional

Ransomware crews are increasingly relying on social engineering and stolen-data extortion instead of encrypting systems, especially targeting law firms and other data-sensitive mid-market organizations. Because paying for a promise to delete data offers little protection from leaks or repeat extortion, organizations should prioritize identity defenses, incident coordination, and recoverable operations.

  • The Silent Ransom Group leak showed that some extortion actors have moved away from widespread file encryption toward stealing data from cloud and software-service environments, using social engineering and targeted insider activity.
  • The article warns that senior law-firm partners are being targeted with tailored emails and phone calls based on information published on their firms’ profile pages.
  • In Q3 2026, the median ransom payment was $400,000, up 167% from Q2 2026, while the average payment fell 45% to $1,025,278.
  • Phishing and social engineering accounted for about 29% of initial access methods in Q3 2026, followed by compromised remote access at 22–23% and compromised credentials at 14–15%.
  • Nearly 80% of data-exfiltration-only incidents were resolved without a ransom payment, as victims increasingly view payment as offering no verifiable assurance that stolen data will be deleted.

Vendors: veeam, coveware

item.title: CVE-2026-111497 Exploited Brotli Flaw Threatens Unpatched .NET Runtimes
item.content:encoded:
Window: 28 Oct 11:00 → 28 Oct 15:00 UTC (4 hours)

Emerging Threat: (CVE-2026-111497) .NET and ASP.NET Core Memory Corruption — Must Read

CVE-2026-111497 is a critical out-of-bounds write in the Google Brotli decoder that can corrupt memory when untrusted Brotli data is decompressed, affecting unpatched .NET, Node.js, and other runtimes. Organizations should urgently update .NET to 8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14, or 11 RC3 and disable Brotli decompression paths where patching is not yet complete.

  • CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write flaw in the Google Brotli decompression library that can allow memory reading or corruption through a crafted Brotli stream.
  • The issue affects unpatched .NET 8, 9, 10, and pre-RC3 .NET 11 releases when applications decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data, while .NET Framework is not affected.
  • Microsoft released fixes in .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14, and 11 RC3 on 25 October 2026.
  • CISA added CVE-2026-111497 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 27 October 2026, with reported exploitation so far focused on Node.js.
  • Organizations should update affected runtimes and, until patching is complete, remove or block Brotli decompression for untrusted requests, HTTP responses, and application inputs.

Technologies: web-server

Products: google-brotli, dotnet, aspnet-core, kestrel, httpclient, brotlistream, brotlidecoder, nativeaot

Vendors: google, microsoft, nodejs, red-hat

item.title: Intelbras Camera DoS Flaw and Aikido External Pentesting Launch
item.content:encoded:
Window: 28 Oct 07:00 → 28 Oct 11:00 UTC (4 hours)

Millions of security cameras at risk: DoS vulnerability in Intelbras devices — May Read

Intelbras patched an unauthenticated firmware-update endpoint in several Mibo IP camera models that let anyone on the local network repeatedly force cameras offline. Users should update to firmware R.260804 to mitigate the denial-of-service flaw.

  • Researchers identified an unauthenticated firmware-update endpoint in Intelbras IP camera firmware that could be used by someone on the local Wi-Fi network to force a camera offline.
  • The issue affected firmware v240927 on the Intelbras iM3B-C and, according to Intelbras, the same firmware was compatible with the iMX C, iM4 C, iM5 SC, iME 360 C, and iM7+ FC models.
  • Sending a firmware upload request triggered the camera reboot process even when the supplied firmware was not valid, and periodic requests could keep the device offline indefinitely.
  • Intelbras released firmware R.260804, which adds checks for authentication session and cookie data before allowing firmware updates through the affected endpoint.
  • MITRE assigned the issue candidate ID CAN-2026-2035970 and classified it as medium severity with a CVSS 4.0 score of 5.1, pending final CVE assignment.

Technologies: iot-device

Products: mibo-smart, im3b-c, imx-c, im4-c, im5-sc, ime-360-c, im7-fc, r-260804

Vendors: intelbras

Aikido launches external network pentesting — Optional

Aikido has launched an AI-powered external network pentesting service that continuously discovers and tests internet-facing assets under a customer’s domain. The service aims to identify and validate exploitable weaknesses safely, providing evidence-backed findings and retesting as the external perimeter changes.

  • Aikido launched an external network pentesting service that maps and tests publicly reachable systems under a customer’s domain using AI agents.
  • The service discovers internet-facing assets such as websites, APIs, VPN gateways, mail servers, and self-hosted tools, while filtering out services the customer does not own.
  • Aikido says its agents test hosts for known CVEs, misconfigurations, and exposed secrets, and only report findings that are supported by validated and reproduced evidence.
  • The service can run continuously so newly discovered hosts are tested shortly after they go live, and its pricing is based on the number of publicly accessible assets found.
  • Aikido states that agents operate with safeguards including action review, limits on deeper exploitation, ownership checks, no downloading or storing customer data, and an emergency stop button.

Products: aikido-external-network-pentesting

Vendors: aikido

Fukuoka Jisho Deploys Netskope Across Seven Group Companies to Deliver Secure Access Anywhere, Powered by SSE — Optional

Fukuoka Jisho has deployed Netskope’s Security Service Edge platform across seven group companies to provide secure, consistent access to applications and data from any location.

  • Fukuoka Jisho deployed Netskope across seven group companies.
  • The deployment is intended to deliver secure access from any location.
  • The initiative is powered by Security Service Edge (SSE) technology.

Technologies: casb, dlp, proxy, remote-access

Products: netskope-one-sse

Vendors: netskope

item.title: INJ3CTOR3 FreePBX Implant Exfiltrates SIP Trunk Credentials
item.content:encoded:
Window: 28 Oct 03:00 → 28 Oct 07:00 UTC (4 hours)

From Hijacked PBX to Stolen Trunk: INJ3CTOR3’s Campaign Evolves — Should Read

INJ3CTOR3’s updated FreePBX malware now exfiltrates SIP trunk, AMI, database, and mail credentials every minute, allowing toll fraud even after an infected PBX is rebuilt. Organizations must isolate and fully eradicate persistence mechanisms before rotating all exposed credentials, especially SIP trunk secrets.

item.content:encoded:

CVE-2026-111497: Node2Shell / HTTP2Shell Vulnerability May Allow RCE — Must Read

CVE-2026-111497 (Node2Shell/HTTP2Shell) is a critical out-of-bounds write in vulnerable Brotli decoders that may enable remote code execution when applications decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data. Organizations should urgently patch affected runtimes and bundled libraries, rebuild containers, and monitor for malformed Content-Encoding: br requests, crashes, and suspicious child processes or outbound connections.

  • CVE-2026-111497, also called Node2Shell and HTTP2Shell, is a critical out-of-bounds write flaw in Google’s Brotli decoder that can lead to crashes, process-memory disclosure, or remote code execution when attacker-controlled Brotli data is decompressed.
  • The flaw affects multiple products and libraries, including Node.js, Bun, Python Brotli bindings, .NET, Envoy Proxy, Istio, Java brotli4j, libbrotli, curl/libcurl dependencies, and Linux distribution packages.
  • Attackers may reach a vulnerable decoder by sending Brotli-compressed HTTP requests with Content-Encoding: br to a server or by returning crafted Brotli-compressed responses to a client that automatically decompresses them.
  • Zscaler Deception observed 402 related events from 20 source IP addresses targeting 12 customers during the first 24 hours after public disclosure, with 40% categorized as reconnaissance and 60% as exploitation attempts.
  • Organizations should patch affected runtimes and libraries, rebuild and redeploy containers using patched components, disable Brotli decoding on vulnerable paths when patching is delayed, and investigate crashes or unusual activity following compressed-input handling.

Technologies: proxy

Products: google-brotli, nodejs, bun, dotnet, envoy-proxy, istio, brotli4j, libbrotli, curl, zscaler-private-access, zscaler-deception

Inside KeyDrift: Analyzing historical UAT-11473 activity on Cisco SD-WAN — Must Read

Cisco Talos found that UAT-11473 exploited CVE-2026-20127 in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN controllers to deploy the KeyDrift malware framework, which persists inside legitimate controller processes and steals sensitive SD-WAN keying material. Organizations should urgently patch affected systems and investigate for modified runit services, injected vdaemon modules, and related post-compromise artifacts.

  • Cisco Talos reported that UAT-11473 exploited CVE-2026-20127, an authentication bypass flaw in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controller instances, to gain unauthorized access.
  • The actor deployed the KeyDrift framework, including PolyFlame and LittleFilch, to maintain access within Cisco SD-WAN controller processes and collect sensitive keying information.
  • PolyFlame is injected into legitimate vdaemon processes and provides command execution and an intermediate command-and-control capability through Cisco SD-WAN control-plane traffic.
  • LittleFilch hooks the SSL_read function in vdaemon, extracts specified control-session fields and assessed AES-256 IPsec data-plane key material, and stores RSA-encrypted records in /var/tmp/vdaemon.bin.
  • Cisco released patches for CVE-2026-20127 and a Catalyst SD-WAN hardening guide, while Talos recommends monitoring for post-compromise activity and activating incident response if unauthorized activity is found.

Technologies: router

PHP2Shell is in CISA KEV: why runtime visibility matters — Must Read

CISA added the actively exploited PHP2Shell flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, to its KEV catalog, making rapid identification and patching of affected PHP runtimes urgent. Organizations need runtime-level inventory to find vulnerable host packages, container images, and managed deployments, then upgrade, rebuild, restart workers, and review systems left exposed.

  • CISA added CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, known as PHP2Shell, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 26, 2026, with a remediation deadline of October 29 for U.S. federal civilian agencies.
  • The affected PHP releases are versions before 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12, while PHP 8.1 and older are end of life and receive no fixes from the PHP project.
  • PHP states that installations serving web requests are at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed, with mod_php carrying the highest risk.
  • Delft University’s Threat Intelligence Lab recorded more than 60,000 PHP2Shell exploitation requests from over 600 IP addresses across more than 70 countries as of October 27.
  • Organizations should identify affected hosts, container images, and managed hosting environments; apply vendor fixes or upgrade PHP; rebuild and redeploy images; and restart PHP workers after updating.

AMOS Malware in AI Agent Skills: Analysis and IoCs — Should Read

Cyera found 516 poisoned AI agent skills distributing Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS), often through fake setup requirements that instruct users or agents to decode and execute malicious payloads. High automated security grades failed to detect these threats, so organizations should inspect entire skill packages and block untrusted installation commands and external dependencies.

  • Cyera Research identified 516 samples associated with an Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS) campaign distributed through poisoned AI agent skills.
  • The malicious skills used fake prerequisites and setup instructions to direct users or agents to download and run credential-stealing malware, with separate payloads for macOS and Windows.
  • The campaign heavily reused the IP address 91.92.242.30 as a payload host and two glot.io snippets that accounted for 95.9% of paste-relay references.
  • All 70 confirmed-malicious skills identified on platforms using automated evaluation received high security grades, indicating that those checks missed malicious instructions embedded in skill files.
  • The article recommends examining complete skill packages and their external dependencies because malicious content can appear in companion files or external resources rather than only in SKILL.md.

Inside Qilin ransomware: ESXi attacks, affiliate networks and double extortion — Should Read

Qilin is a highly active Russian-speaking ransomware-as-a-service operation whose affiliates use phishing, stolen credentials, exposed systems and remote-management tools to steal data and encrypt Windows, network and VMware ESXi environments. Its configurable tooling disables recovery and security controls, supports double extortion, and makes healthcare and other organizations significant targets.

  • Qilin, also known as Agenda, is a Russian-speaking ransomware-as-a-service operation active since 2022 that claimed more than 1,000 victims in 2025.
  • Qilin affiliates commonly gain access through targeted phishing, compromised VPN or RDP credentials, vulnerable internet-facing applications, and remote-management tools.
  • The group uses double extortion by encrypting systems while threatening to publish stolen data if victims do not pay.
  • Qilin can encrypt local files, network shares, domain environments, and VMware ESXi infrastructure, and its ESXi-focused PowerShell script can enable SSH and deploy encryption payloads to hosts.
  • In 2024, a Qilin attack on U.K. diagnostic provider Synnovis disrupted services at several London hospitals, affected thousands of medical procedures, and exposed data on approximately 900,000 individuals.

Technologies: hypervisor, operating-system, edr, xdr, backup

Products: qilin, windows, powershell, vmware-esxi, vmware-vcenter, powercli, acronis-edr, acronis-xdr

Vendors: acronis, microsoft, vmware

Malicious AI Skills: The Risk to Corporate Endpoints — May Read

Cyera researchers found a trojanized copy of Anthropic’s PDF skill that preserved legitimate files and metadata but replaced its instructions and added an obfuscated Linux reverse-shell binary. The case highlights how AI-agent skills can become a supply-chain risk and should be fully verified before installation or execution.

  • Cyera Research analyzed a package named “pdf” that imitated Anthropic’s official PDF skill by retaining the same name, description, and 11 identical files.
  • The package replaced the original 315-line SKILL.md with a 19-line file containing a command to contact scan.100tal[.]com and added an obfuscated 64-bit Linux executable named system_linux.
  • The system_linux binary is a statically linked Go program that decrypts the hard-coded destination 81.70.101[.]115:2345 and, if run, connects over plain TCP and attaches /bin/bash to that connection.
  • Researchers observed five similar tar files from May 23 to July 14, 2026, but could not establish how they were distributed, whether anyone installed them, or whether the binary was executed.
  • The article advises organizations to verify an entire skill package against its claimed source and investigate unexpected commands, network destinations, and executable files before allowing an AI agent to use it.

Technologies: cloud-platform, operating-system

Products: anthropic-pdf-skill, claude-code, claude-cowork, agent-guardian, garble, tencent-cloud

Vendors: anthropic, cyera, tencent

The Phishing Email That Shipped Its Own Clean Verdicts — May Read

A phishing email impersonating Mailgun embedded dozens of forged email-security headers claiming clean authentication and low spam risk, but the only trusted receiving hop showed SPF softfail, DKIM failure, and DMARC failure. Defenders should treat headers added below their trusted mail boundary as attacker-controlled text rather than evidence.

  • A plain-text email impersonating a Mailgun account notice included roughly 70 sender-written headers that falsely claimed low spam risk, internal authentication, passing authentication checks, and a passing ARC seal.
  • The only trusted receiving hop recorded a DKIM body-hash failure, SPF softfail, DMARC failure, and a non-contiguous ARC chain.
  • The forged Exchange antispam headers named mail.contoso.com, Microsoft's documentation placeholder domain, while another forged header used the impossible IP address 541.428.412.821.
  • A planted ARC seal's signature value base64-decoded to the decimal number 0.49584384000973525 rather than a cryptographic signature.
  • IRONSCALES Themis identified a first-time sender and malicious link, and automated detection quarantined both waves of the campaign.

Technologies: email-security, cloud-platform

Products: themis, microsoft-exchange, gmail, azure-front-door, mailgun

Vendors: ironscales, microsoft, google, mailgun

Millions of security cameras at risk: DoS vulnerability in Intelbras devices — May Read

Intelbras patched an unauthenticated firmware-update endpoint in several Mibo IP camera models that let anyone on the local network repeatedly force cameras offline. Users should update to firmware R.260804 to mitigate the denial-of-service flaw.

  • Researchers identified an unauthenticated firmware-update endpoint in Intelbras IP camera firmware that could be used by someone on the local Wi-Fi network to force a camera offline.
  • The issue affected firmware v240927 on the Intelbras iM3B-C and, according to Intelbras, the same firmware was compatible with the iMX C, iM4 C, iM5 SC, iME 360 C, and iM7+ FC models.
  • Sending a firmware upload request triggered the camera reboot process even when the supplied firmware was not valid, and periodic requests could keep the device offline indefinitely.
  • Intelbras released firmware R.260804, which adds checks for authentication session and cookie data before allowing firmware updates through the affected endpoint.
  • MITRE assigned the issue candidate ID CAN-2026-2035970 and classified it as medium severity with a CVSS 4.0 score of 5.1, pending final CVE assignment.

The Silent Ransom Group Leak Shows Why Paying for Silence Fails — Optional

Ransomware crews are increasingly relying on social engineering and stolen-data extortion instead of encrypting systems, especially targeting law firms and other data-sensitive mid-market organizations. Because paying for a promise to delete data offers little protection from leaks or repeat extortion, organizations should prioritize identity defenses, incident coordination, and recoverable operations.

  • The Silent Ransom Group leak showed that some extortion actors have moved away from widespread file encryption toward stealing data from cloud and software-service environments, using social engineering and targeted insider activity.
  • The article warns that senior law-firm partners are being targeted with tailored emails and phone calls based on information published on their firms’ profile pages.
  • In Q3 2026, the median ransom payment was $400,000, up 167% from Q2 2026, while the average payment fell 45% to $1,025,278.
  • Phishing and social engineering accounted for about 29% of initial access methods in Q3 2026, followed by compromised remote access at 22–23% and compromised credentials at 14–15%.
  • Nearly 80% of data-exfiltration-only incidents were resolved without a ransom payment, as victims increasingly view payment as offering no verifiable assurance that stolen data will be deleted.

Aikido has launched an AI-agent-based external network pentesting service that continuously discovers and tests internet-facing assets under a customer’s domain. Effective SOC analysts need foundational skills across operating systems, networking, logs, endpoint detection, incident response, threat hunting, malware and memory analysis, automation, and communication. The key is connecting evidence across these domains to identify and respond to threats effectively.

item.title: FBI Seizes Virtualine.net in Operation Omegaline Targeting Omegatech
item.content:encoded:
Window: 27 Oct 19:00 → 27 Oct 23:00 UTC (4 hours)

Omegatech Is Disrupted, and the Pressure on Bulletproof Hosting Keeps Building — Should Read

Law enforcement’s seizure of Virtualine/Omegatech reflects growing pressure on bulletproof hosting providers, but these operators can rapidly evade disruption by shifting IP ranges and customers to new ASNs and shell companies. Defenders should continuously track infrastructure patterns, newly populated ASNs, and sanctions-linked entities rather than relying on static blocklists.

  • The FBI seized virtualine.net on October 27, 2026, under Operation Omegaline, following an investigation led by the FBI Washington Field Office with law-enforcement partners in Germany, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom.
  • Silent Push observed infrastructure moving from Railnet LLC (AS214943) to Omegatech (AS202412) in February 2026 and identified Virtualine Technologies within Omegatech’s network.
  • Omegatech was not fully offline after the seizure, but its network address ranges showed very low routing visibility, which the article says typically indicates a serious operator-side problem.
  • In 2026, authorities also seized more than 800 servers associated with THE.Hosting/WorkTitans BV and arrested two men, while the EU sanctioned Media Land, ML Cloud, and general director Aleksandr Volosovik.
  • The article states that bulletproof hosting providers can obtain a new network identifier within two to five business days and move the same malicious internet address ranges to it, making static blocklists quickly outdated.

Technologies: cloud-platform, network-monitoring

Products: silent-push-platform, iofa-bulletproof-hosting-feed

Vendors: silent-push, omegatech, virtualine-technologies, railnet, the-hosting, aeza-group, media-land
